content: Dactylis is a genus of grasses that belongs to the subfamily Pooideae. These grasses are native to Europe, Asia, and northern Africa. In English, they are commonly referred to as cock's-foot or cocksfoot grasses, and occasionally as orchard grasses. The genus Dactylis has historically been considered by many authors to consist of only a single species, Dactylis glomerata. Variations within the genus were often classified at the subspecific level within D. glomerata. However, more recent studies have led to the recognition of two distinct species within the genus, with some authors even identifying additional species, particularly those endemic to islands in Macaronesia. The grasses in this genus are characterized by their distinctive triangular, tufted flower heads, which form a panicle measuring 10–15 cm in length. These flower heads turn pale grey-brown when the seeds mature. The spikelets are 5–9 mm long and typically contain two to five flowers. The stems of these grasses have a flattened base, which sets them apart from many other grass species. The recognized species within the genus include: Dactylis glomerata L., which is found throughout most of the genus's range. Dactylis marina Borrill, native to the western Mediterranean region, including southwestern Europe and northwestern Africa. Dactylis metlesicsii Schönfelder & Ludwig, an endemic species of the Canary Islands. Dactylis smithii Link (synonym: D. glomerata subsp. smithii (Link) Stebbins & Zohary), which is found in the Canary Islands, Cape Verde, and Madeira. Cytological studies of the genus reveal varying levels of polyploidy among its taxa. For example, Dactylis glomerata subsp. glomerata and D. glomerata subsp. hispanica are tetraploid forms, each possessing 28 chromosomes. Other taxa, such as D. glomerata subsp. himalayensis (synonym: D. himalayensis), D. glomerata subsp. lobata (synonym: D. polygama), D. metlesicsii, and some forms of D. smithii, are diploid with 2n = 14 chromosomes. Rarely, hexaploid forms with 42 chromosomes have also been observed.
